(1) we introduce inclusive-NRF, a new approach to learn NRFs with inclusive divergence minimized auxiliary generators, (2) inclusive-NRFs are theoretically examined to be capable of exploiting gradient information in sampling, and (3) inclusive-NRF is empirically shown to represent the best-performing random field on a wide range of image generation and semi- supervised classification tasks

(i) we develop a new family of neural random fields with inclusive-divergences minimized auxiliary generators, (ii) we show that the proposed inclusive-NRF approach can be applied in unsupervised and semi-supervised learning tasks and achieves state-of-the-art performance on CIFAR-100, SVHN and MNIST datasets, and (iii) we provide solid theoretical examination on the proposed approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a new class of random fields for machine learning and we believe that our work will provide useful insights for future studies in random fields and generative modeling.

the design and learning of a class of random fields that are capable of generating high quality samples from complex data distributions, and at the same time, are capable of learning from data with only limited supervision.

the following questions: (1) how to use gradient information in NRFs for model sampling; (2) how to use NRFs in semi-supervised learning; and (3) how to use inclusive-divergence minimization for learning NRFs with gradient information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

inclusive-NRF provides the best of both worlds - the best semi-supervised classification results and the best unsupervised generation results, among all generative models, and the best semi-supervision and generation results among random fields.

inclusive-NRF is the best-performed NRF for image generation, and is competitive to state-of-the-art methods for semi-supervised classification on the three datasets, and is the only method that achieves the best performance in both tasks.
, inclusive-NRF is a promising approach to NRF learning, and has great potentials in both semi-supervised learning and generative modeling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inclusive-NRF is a powerful model for image generation and classification, and is an interesting alternative to the recently popularized variational inference based methods.

, we develop a new learning framework for random fields with neural potential functions, and provide empirical evidence that the resulting inclusive-NRFs outperform previous random fields and generative model based methods in unsupervised image generation, and in semi-supervised classification with superior generation quality.
inclusive-NRF is a promising new model family that is able to achieve state-of-the art performance in unsupervised and semi-supervised image generation, and semi-supervised learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by using a well-designed auxiliary generator, the gradient information in the auxiliary generator can be effectively exploited for model sampling, which leads to better performance than previous approaches that do not exploit such information.
the inclusive-NRFs are a promising family of models for unsupervised/super-vized image generation, as well as semi-supervised classification.
inclusive-divergence minimization can help us to learn more flexible NRFs, which are capable of generating high-quality images.
